summary: Detects CPUID support by toggling the EFLAGS ID bit (0x200000) and reading EFLAGS back. If the write sticks (v0 != v1), CPUID is supported: runs CPUID with EAX=1 and returns bit 23 of EDX (mask 0x800000), the MMX feature flag. Otherwise returns the XOR of the two EFLAGS snapshots (0 when unchanged).

operations.description: Read current EFLAGS into v0 via __readeflags().
Write EFLAGS with the ID bit toggled: __writeeflags(v0 ^ 0x200000).
Read EFLAGS again into v1 and compute v2 = v0 ^ v1.
If v0 != v1 the ID bit is writable, so CPUID is supported; otherwise return v2 (0).
Set EAX = 1 and execute the CPUID instruction.
Return (EDX & 0x800000) >> 23: bit 23 of CPUID.1:EDX, the MMX feature flag.
Return v2 (= 0) when the EFLAGS ID bit is not writable.

unresolved: The literal 0x800000 is rendered by the decompiler as the address unk_800000 (0x00800000); semantically it is a bitmask on EDX bit 23 (MMX), not a real memory dereference.
The MMX labeling of bit 23 is standard CPUID interpretation and DERIVED, not confirmed by the packet alone.
The owner and the CPU feature consumer at caller sub_50F632 are unknown.
